newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - July 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - July 15.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- MING PAO -- More than 300 illegal immigrant children from mainland China have applied for legal aid to fight for their right of abode in Hong Kong.

-- EXPRESS NEWS -- It is almost certain China's Vice-Premier Zhu Rongji will replace Li Peng as premier during the 15th Communist Party congress in September. But it is not clear whether the position of party chairman will be revived according to the wishes of President Jiang Zemin.

-- APPLE DAILY -- Police internal instructions on how to handle cases involving the People's Liberation Army (PLA) garrison in Hong Kong says officers cannot enter PLA premises to detain staff or search uniformed soldiers.

-- TIN TIN DAILY -- A centre for destroying old banknotes will be completed in Shenzhen next month. China has said that 70 percent of notes in circulation will be new ones by the end of the century. In the southern province of Guangdong alone, old notes worth 72 billion yuan will have to be destroyed.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Rex International Development Co Ltd, labelled as a threat to Hong Kong's security for allegedly helping Iran produce "weapons of mass destruction", has challenged a government decision to close down the company.

-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- Hong Kong Monetary Authority chief executive Joseph Yam urged the region's central banks to make a more concerted effort to check rampant speculative attacks on Asian currencies.
